chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The Day when the earth shall be changed into a different earth.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It shall be changed into a pure bread. The people will eat from it until they are finished with the Reckoning.'

So a speaker said to him: 'They are in an occupation on that Day from eating and drinking.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the son of Adam hollow, and there is no escape for him from food and drink. Are they more occupied on that Day, or those in the Fire?'
So they cry for help, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Saying: 'And if they cry for help, they shall be given water like molten brass which will scald their faces; evil is the drink.'
ai.seo_question: What does the 'changed earth' refer to in Shia interpretation of the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi offers a nuanced interpretation of Surah Ibrahim 14:48, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'changing the earth' refers to the provision of pure sustenance during the intense preoccupation of the reckoning, affirming human physiological needs even in the afterlife. The Imam contrasts the believers' consumption with the inhabitants of Hell, who are similarly occupied but cry for water only to receive scalding molten brass, a detail explicitly linked to the verse in Surah Ibrahim. This highlights the dual reality of the Day of Judgment where spiritual focus does not negate physical necessity for the righteous.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from al Wasim Bin Urwat, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [14:48] The Day when the earth shall be Changed into a different earth. Heasws said: ‘It would be changed into pure bread. The people would be eating from it until they are free from the Reckoning’.

So a speaker said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘They would be in an occupation on that Day (too pre-occupied) from the eating and the drinking’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Created the son of Adam<sup>as</sup> as hollow, and there is no escape for him from the food and the drink. Would they be in a more intense occupation on that Day or the ones in the Fire?

So they would be crying for it, and Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [18:29] and if they cry for water, they shall be given water like molten brass which will scald their faces; evil is the drink’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from al-Qasim ibn al-’Urwah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘On the day when the earth will be replaced with another earth.’ [14:48] He (the Imam) said, ‘It will be replaced with purified bread from which people will eat until their accounting is complete.’

Someone then said to him (the Imam), ‘People on that day will already have other things to worry about instead of eating.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has created the child of Adam hollow. He must have food and drink. Will they be more seriously preoccupied on that day or those in hellfire who plead?
And Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, “If they plead their pleading will be responded with water like al-Muhl that roasts the faces and it is the worst kind of drink.” [18:29]’”
